chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Sawwar, from Al-Hasan, who said:

Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him), when he defeated Talha and Al-Zubayr, the people turned in retreat. They passed by a pregnant woman on the road, so she panicked from them and cast out what was in her belly alive. It struggled until it died, then its mother died after it.

So Ali (peace be upon him) and his companions passed by her, and she was lying there with her child on the road. He asked them about her matter, so they said to him, 'Indeed, she was pregnant; she panicked when she saw the fighting and the defeat.'
He said, 'So he asked them, which of the two died before its companion?' So it was said, 'Her son died before her.'

He said, 'So he called her husband, the father of the dead boy, and made him inherit from his son two-thirds of the wergild (blood money). And he made the mother inherit one-third of the wergild. Then he made the husband inherit from his dead wife half of the one-third wergild which she had inherited from her son, and he made the relatives of the dead woman inherit the remainder.'

Then he made the husband inherit also from the wergild of his dead wife, half of the wergild, which was two thousand and five hundred dirhams. And he made the relatives of the dead woman inherit half of the wergild, which was two thousand and five hundred dirhams. And that is because there was no child for her other than that which she cast out when she panicked.
He said, 'And he paid all of that from the Public Treasury of Al-Basra.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْغُلَام: Father of the boy (a kunya used for the husband)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Wergild or blood money compensation paid for death or injury
key_terms.قَرَابَةَ الْمَرْأَة: The relatives of the woman (maternal/paternal kin)

ai.seo_question: How is blood money distributed when a pregnant woman and her unborn child both die?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) sophisticated application of inheritance law during the Battle of Siffin, specifically addressing the legal status of a fetus who dies before the mother. It establishes that the mother inherits from the live-born fetus, and the husband inherits from the mother, demonstrating a nuanced understanding of simultaneous death and contingent inheritance in Shia fiqh. The ruling was paid from the public treasury (Bayt al-Mal), highlighting the state's role in compensating for such complex casualties.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Sawwar, from Al Hassan who said,

‘When Ali<sup>asws</sup> defeated Talha and Al-Zubeyr, the people faced their defeat, so they passed by a pregnant woman upon the road. So she panicked from them, and gave birth to what was in her belly, alive. So it (child) became restless until it died. Then its mother died from after it.

So Ali<sup>asws</sup> and his companions passed by her and she and her child were lying upon the road. So he<sup>asws</sup> told them about her matter, so they said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘But rather, she was pregnant, so she panicked when she saw the fighting and the defeat’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> asked them, ‘Which of the two died before its companion?’ So it was said, ‘Her son died before her’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> called her husband, father of the dead boy, so made him to inherit from his son, two-thirds of the wergild (blood money compensation), and her mother to inherit a third of the wergild. Then made the husband to inherit from his dead wife, half of the one-third wergild which she had inherited from her son, and made the relatives of the dead woman, the remainder (of the one-third wergild).

Then made the husband to inherit as well from the wergild of the dead woman, half of the wergild, and it was two thousand and five hundred Dirhams, and made the relatives of the dead woman to inherit half of the wergild, and it was two thousand and five hundred Dirhams, and that is because there did not happen to be for her any child other than that which had been miscarried with when she panicked.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> paid all of that from the Public Treasury of Al-Basra’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father all from ibn Mahbub from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Sawwar from al-Hassan who has narrated the following:

“When Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, defeated Talhah and al-Zubayr, people came defeated and passed by a pregnant woman on the road who was frightened and miscarried her child who was alive but then died. She, because of shock died after the child.

Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and his people passed by where she with her child was left on the road. He (the Imam) asked them about her case and they said that she was pregnant. Because of shock on seeing the dead and defeated she has died.
He (the Imam) then asked, ’Who died first?’ They said, ’The child died before her.’

He (the Imam) called her husband and made him to inherit his son for two-thirds of the wergild and the mother to inherit one-third of the wergild. He (the Imam) made the man to inherit from his dead wife one-half of the one-third, which she had inherited of the wergild of her son. The relatives of the dead woman inherited the remaining.

He (the Imam) then made the husband to inherit also from the wergild of the dead woman, one-half which is two thousand and five hundred dirham. He (the Imam) allowed the relatives of the dead woman to inherit the other one-half, which was two thousand and five hundred dirham. This is because she did not have any children other than that whom she miscarried because of shock.
He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) paid all of it from the public treasury of Basrah.’”
